steps.message:
# Some coins misbehave in the flooded cave

### What happens
`recording.mp4` is an uncut run through a flooded cave basin. Partway through the clip, Tux does something that releases a group of new coins. From that moment until the end of the clip, those coins do not behave the way coins in this game should. The coins that were already placed in the level, Tux, the fish and the scenery in the recording are correct.

### Expected
The released coins should behave correctly for as long as they are on screen. Once a coin is in the water it should drift down slowly, however hard it hit the surface. It should take a coin about three seconds to sink the height of the tallest thing growing on the basin floor. Fix every way the released coins behave wrongly in the recording.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4` (44 seconds)

You can inspect individual moments of the video by extracting frames from it with `ffmpeg`.

Inspect the attached file before making changes.

steps.message:
I couldn't watch the recording: `/app/.harbor_assets/` is empty and there's no `recording.mp4` anywhere on the system. So I worked from the code instead. A group of new coins released by Tux means `CoinExplode`, which spawns `HeavyCoin` objects (from an exploding bonus block or a gold bomb). I found and fixed two bugs there. The build succeeds, but I haven't run the game to watch the coins.

**1. The coin fan was mirrored the wrong way** (`src/object/coin_explode.cpp`)
Each coin velocity is meant to be used twice, once flipped left-to-right. The code flipped the vertical part instead (`Vector(vector.x, vector.y * side)`). As a result, all 10 coins flew to the right and half of them shot straight down instead of up. It's now `Vector(vector.x * side, vector.y)`, so you get the symmetric upward fan.

**2. Released coins ignored water** (`HeavyCoin::update` in `src/object/coin.cpp`)
These coins fell at full gravity through water. Now, while a coin overlaps a water tile:
- Gravity is turned off, and the coin's downward speed is capped right away at the sink speed. A coin that hits the surface hard drops to a slow drift straight away.
- Water drag smooths any other motion (sideways, or upward from a burst underwater) towards a steady downward drift.
- The sink speed is 128/3 ≈ 43 px/s, so a coin takes about 3 seconds to sink the height of a full seaweed plant (4 tiles, 128 px). Seaweed is the tallest plant in the tileset, but because I couldn't see the video I can't confirm it's the tallest thing on that basin's floor. If something taller grows there, `WATER_SINK_SPEED` needs adjusting.
- Sinking follows the sector's gravity direction, so it still works in flipped-gravity levels.
- Once out of the water, normal gravity applies again.

I also read the other coin code paths (collecting, bouncing off solid tiles, the gold bomb and bonus block spawn sites) and found nothing else wrong. If you can re-attach the recording, I'll check the fixes against it, especially in case it shows a problem I couldn't infer from the code.
